candidates.attacker_control: A remote unauthenticated attacker controls the HTTP request path (e.g., `GET /img/../../../../etc/app/config.properties HTTP/1.1`). The path is decoded by URI.getPath() in WebContextBase.path() (percent-encoded '.'/'/' such as %2e%2e%2f also decode into '..' '/' there), and ctx.pathNew() is used directly by the static handler; no application privilege or prior state is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for any existing '..'/canonical-path/allow-list check across the repository (searched getCanonicalPath, normalize, traversal, '..' patterns): none exists in the static-file path. Confirmed WebContextBase.path() only collapses duplicate slashes and does not resolve '..'. Confirmed the default mapping is classpath-based and generally not filesystem-traversable, so a filesystem repository mapping is required. Confirmed servlet containers/some proxies normalize dot segments, which reduces exposure. Confirmed the suffix/extension requirement limits target file names. Confirmed no runtime verification was performed; behavior depends on the concrete server/connector and configuration.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file read within the permissions of the application process: configuration files with credentials/keys, environment files, source artifacts adjacent to the static root, etc. This is a direct confidentiality breach that can enable further compromise (e.g., reading datasource/JWT/vault secrets). It is an unauthenticated, network-reachable primitive in deployments using a filesystem static mapping and a non-normalizing server/proxy.
candidates.prerequisites: (1) A filesystem-backed static mapping must be configured (solon.staticfiles.mappings with a repository path, or ExtendStaticRepository) - a documented, first-class use case shown in the module README; in debug mode ClassPathStaticRepository also falls back to a filesystem directory and is equally affected. (2) The front end must pass dot segments through to Solon (Solon's built-in jdkhttp/jlhttp/smarthttp context classes do not normalize; servlet containers such as Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow and normalizing reverse proxies may reject/resolve them). (3) The target file must contain a '.' after the last '/' (StaticResourceHandler.findByExtName requirements), which is true for .properties/.yml/.json/.env/.pem/.key/.java/.jar-like names, and any extension is accepted because Utils.mime() falls back to application/octet-stream.
candidates.root_cause: StaticResourceHandler takes the request path from ctx.pathNew() and passes it to StaticMappings.find(), which only checks a path-prefix match (path.startsWith(m.pathPrefix)) and then hands the remaining, attacker-controlled relative path to the repository. FileStaticRepository.find()/ExtendStaticRepository.find() do `new File(location, relativePath)` and serve the file if it exists, with no rejection of '.'/'..' segments, no canonicalization, and no check that the resolved file stays under the repository root. WebContextBase.path() only collapses duplicate '/' characters (Utils.trimDuplicates) and never resolves dot segments, so a raw request path such as `/mapped/../../../../opt/app/config.properties` survives intact when Solon's own lightweight servers are used.
candidates.title: Path traversal in solon-web-staticfiles filesystem repositories allows arbitrary file read
candidates.trace: ctx.pathNew() (WebContextBase.path(), no '..' resolution) -> StaticResourceHandler.handle() line 52/97 -> StaticMappings.find() line 72 prefix check, line 86 path.substring(prefix) -> FileStaticRepository.find() line 59 new File(location, relativePath) -> line 61 file.exists() -> line 62 file.toURI().toURL() -> StaticResourceHandler line 145 OutputUtils.outputFile(...) -> OutputUtils.outputFile(Context, URL, ...) line 139/145/151 reads and writes the file to the HTTP response (also reachable via the path + '.gz'/'.br' branches at lines 80-92).
candidates.unverified: Runtime exploitability could not be confirmed (no code execution/tests allowed). Whether a given deployment is affected depends on the configured static mappings, the chosen HTTP server/proxy's path normalization, and the presence of a target file with an extension; only source-level evidence establishes the missing validation and the reachable join of untrusted path data onto a filesystem root.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

coverage_summary: Scope: all 2,493 model-visible files under the assigned source root (no path/name exclusions or binary skips reported by get_source_scope). Inspected: solon core Context/route/handler/Gateway/PathMatcher/PathRule/Utils, solon-mvc parameter binding, boot-web contexts (jdkhttp, jlhttp, smarthttp, jetty, undertow, vertx, websocket/netty), web-staticfiles, web-webdav, solon-security-auth/validation/vault, web-cors, sessionstate-local/jwt/jedis, serialization modules (jackson, jackson-xml, fastjson, fastjson2, fury, kryo, hessian, abc, properties), nami coders/channels, solon-data cache/datasource/sql, solon-cloud-gateway, health detector, faas-luffy, native/aot, maven/gradle tooling, and the __test demo app. Not exhaustively read: large solon-data/sqlink code, solon-cloud internals (event/config), view templates, scheduling, docs generators, and much of solon-tool/solon-native. Findings are source-level only.
limitations: No code execution, tests, servers, or exploit payloads were run, so no finding is runtime-confirmed.

Exploitability of the selected path-traversal candidate depends on deployment configuration (filesystem static mapping) and on whether the HTTP front end (container/proxy or Solon's own server) passes dot segments through unnormalized; this was reasoned from source, not observed.
Static reading cannot enumerate which gadget classes or plugins are present in a concrete application, limiting confidence for the rejected deserialization leads.
Coverage was targeted rather than exhaustive across all 2,493 files; areas listed in the coverage summary were sampled or skipped.
The snapshot has no version-control metadata, so I could not compare against upstream fixed revisions or determine whether any specific line was recently changed.

rejected_leads.lead: WebDAV path traversal: solon-web-webdav WebdavAbstractHandler.stripPrefix() (URL-decodes ctx.path and Destination) feeds LocalFileSystem.realPath(), which is `rootPath + "/" + path` with no containment check, allowing traversal for PUT/DELETE/COPY/MOVE (read/write/delete impact).
rejected_leads.reason: Same class of missing path canonicalization but a separate, niche module that must be explicitly wired up (subclass with user()/fileSystem()); not selected as the single strongest candidate to avoid splitting one root cause and because exploitation requires an app custom implementation. Unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe deserialization in serialization modules: JacksonActionExecutor enables default typing with the permissive default PolymorphicTypeValidator on request bodies; FuryBytesSerializer uses requireClassRegistration(false) with only a WARN-level blacklist; KryoBytesSerializer uses setRegistrationRequired(false) + readClassAndObject; Nami fastjson/fastjson2 decoders enable autotype including ParserConfig.getGlobalInstance().setAutoTypeSupport(true).
rejected_leads.reason: These are real CWE-502 hardening concerns, but exploitability depends on library-specific gadget availability, Object/Map-typed action parameters, and opt-in serializer plugins; they read as deliberate (if unsafe) serializer design rather than a single discrete defect, and deserializing a body happens only for the matching Content-Type. Not selected; unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: IP-based access control bypass: AuthRuleImpl/IpInterceptor use ctx.realIp(), and IpUtil.getRealIp() trusts the client-supplied X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For headers before falling back to remoteIp(); solon-web-stop similarly compares the spoofable value to its whitelist.
rejected_leads.reason: Trusting forwarding headers is common and configurable (IpUtil.globalSet), and the stop endpoint is disabled by default; treated as a hardening/configuration concern rather than the strongest discrete vulnerability. Unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: CORS defaults: AbstractCross reflects the request Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true by default, and a configured allow-list is matched with allowedOrigins.contains(origin) (substring) rather than exact origin comparison.
rejected_leads.reason: The reflection is intentional to make wildcard+credentials work; the substring check is only exploitable if the configured allow-list itself contains an attacker-controlled origin substring, so concrete impact is limited. Rejected as a weaker lead.

summary: Reviewed the Solon 3.0.9-M1 snapshot (2,493 readable files) as a static, source-only vulnerability assessment. I traced attacker-controlled request data into framework sinks across the core handler/route chain, the built-in boot servers, serialization modules, static-file/WebDAV file services, auth/IP handling, CORS, session handling, data/cache, and the cloud gateway. The strongest source-evidenced candidate is a path-traversal in the static-file service: the request path (context.pathNew()) is prefix-stripped and passed, unvalidated and un-normalized, to repository implementations that join it onto a configured filesystem root, allowing '..' segments to escape the mapped directory and serve arbitrary extension-bearing files. Other plausible issues (unsafe deserialization in serialization modules, WebDAV 'rootPath + path' traversal, X-Real-IP spoofing for @AuthIp/stop, default CORS reflection with credentials) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads because they depend on additional preconditions or appear to be opt-in design choices. No runtime testing was performed; the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
